content: Atomic JSON writes on Node.js require the write-temp-then-rename pattern: write new content to a sibling temp file in the SAME directory (same filesystem, or rename becomes non-atomic EXDEV copy-then-delete), then fs.rename() over the target. POSIX rename is atomic; readers see old or new content, never partial. For durability against power loss, also fsync the temp file before rename and fsync the parent directory after. A crash mid-plain-writeFile can leave a truncated/empty file.
